name: Adriano Celentano
milestone_by_age_26: Signed to Jolly Records in 1958 and released his first hit singles and debut album by 1960, credited with introducing rock and roll to Italy.
early_history_summary: Born in Milan to working-class parents from Apulia, Celentano worked as a watchmaker before being discovered by Jolly Records A&R executive Ezio Leoni, who signed him to his first recording contract. He released his first singles in 1958 at age 20, had a hit with 'Il tuo bacio è come un rock' in 1959, and released his debut album in 1960. He appeared in Fellini's La Dolce Vita in 1960 and founded his own record label Clan Celentano in 1962 at age 24.
family_context_summary: Parents were from Foggia, Apulia, and had moved north for work; his father was a laborer. No evidence of family wealth or music industry connections.
primary_early_advantage_tags: milan rock and roll scene, ezio leoni mentorship, jolly records contract, elvis presley influence, giorgio gaber peer
evidence_summary: Celentano grew up in Milan during the rock and roll explosion of the 1950s and was inspired by Elvis Presley. He was discovered by Jolly Records A&R executive Ezio Leoni, who signed him and co-authored his early hits. He played in a rock and roll band with Giorgio Gaber and Enzo Jannacci before his solo career took off. His early singles in 1958 and debut album in 1960 made him a pioneer of Italian rock and roll. No evidence of family wealth or music industry connections; his advantage came from being in Milan at the right time and connecting with the right producer.

name: Tim Berners-Lee
milestone_by_age_26: Invented the World Wide Web in 1989 at age 34; while he built the ENQUIRE prototype at CERN in 1980 (age 25), it was a personal, unpublished tool, not a material independently verifiable milestone.
early_history_summary: Born in London to mathematician parents who worked on the Ferranti Mark 1 computer, Berners-Lee studied physics at Oxford, graduating in 1976. He worked at Plessey and D.G. Nash before a six-month stint at CERN in 1980 where he built ENQUIRE, a personal hypertext prototype. He returned to CERN in 1984 and proposed the World Wide Web in 1989.
family_context_summary: Both parents were mathematicians and computer scientists who worked on the Ferranti Mark 1, the first commercially built computer.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents Conway Berners-Lee and Mary Lee Woods were both computer scientists who worked on the Ferranti Mark 1, providing early exposure to computing.

name: Pierre-Gilles de Gennes
milestone_by_age_26: Defended his PhD in 1957 at age 25, creating a complete theory of critical-point behavior in neutron scattering that the Royal Society described as remaining a classic today.
early_history_summary: Born in Paris and home-schooled to age 12, de Gennes entered the École Normale Supérieure in 1951 at age 19. After graduating in 1955, he became a research engineer at the CEA Saclay center, working on neutron scattering and magnetism. He defended his PhD in 1957 at age 25, then did a postdoc at UC Berkeley with Charles Kittel in 1959.
family_context_summary: Home-schooled by his mother until age 12; his father died when he was nine. His maternal grandfather was a descendant of mathematician Jean Bernoulli, suggesting an intellectual lineage. He was sent to Bristol at 13 to learn English.
parent_family_domain_summary: His father died when he was nine. His mother home-schooled him, and the family had intellectual connections including descent from mathematician Jean Bernoulli. The physicist Giuseppe Occhialini, met in Bristol at 13, transmitted his passion for physics.
primary_early_advantage_tags: ecole normale superieure, CEA Saclay, home-schooled, bernoulli lineage, kittel postdoc, neutron scattering theory
evidence_summary: De Gennes was home-schooled until 12 and showed early mathematical talent, entering ENS at 19. He benefited from the elite French academic pipeline (ENS, CEA Saclay) and worked under advisors Anatole Abragam and Jacques Friedel. His PhD at 25 produced a complete theory of critical-point behavior in neutron scattering that remains a classic. His family had intellectual lineage (Bernoulli descendant) and his mother's home-schooling provided an early educational advantage. The loss of his father at age nine may have created urgency.

name: Isamu Akasaki
milestone_by_age_26: By age 26 (1955), Akasaki was a research scientist at Kobe Kogyo Corporation; his Nobel-winning work on blue LEDs began in the late 1960s with the key breakthrough in 1989 at age 60. No material milestone by 26 found.
early_history_summary: Born in Kagoshima, Japan, Akasaki graduated from Kyoto University in 1952 at age 23 and worked as a research scientist at Kobe Kogyo Corporation from 1952 to 1959. He later became a professor at Nagoya University and spent decades researching GaN-based blue LEDs, achieving the breakthrough in 1989.
family_context_summary: His elder brother Masanori Akazaki was an electronic engineering researcher and Professor Emeritus at Kyushu University, suggesting a family with technical aptitude.
parent_family_domain_summary: Elder brother was an electronic engineering professor at Kyushu University, suggesting some family technical environment.

name: Amos Oz
milestone_by_age_26: Published his first book, 'Where the Jackals Howl,' a collection of short stories, in 1965 at age 25-26, receiving immediate critical acclaim.
early_history_summary: Born in Jerusalem to immigrant intellectuals, Oz left home at 14 to join Kibbutz Hulda, where he was allotted time to write. He served in the IDF Nahal Brigade, then studied philosophy and Hebrew literature at Hebrew University, graduating in 1963. He published his first book in 1965 while teaching at the kibbutz high school.
family_context_summary: Born to immigrant parents who met at Hebrew University; his father was a librarian and his mother attended Charles University in Prague. His mother committed suicide when he was 12. His great-uncle Joseph Klausner was a prominent intellectual and Hebrew literature professor.
parent_family_domain_summary: His father studied history and literature and worked as a librarian at the Jewish National and University Library. His great-uncle Joseph Klausner chaired the Hebrew literature department at Hebrew University and hosted intellectual salons. His mother studied history and philosophy at Charles University.
primary_early_advantage_tags: kibbutz self-creation, intellectual family, mother suicide, hebrew university, klausner library, jerusalem literary milieu
evidence_summary: Oz grew up in an impoverished Jerusalem neighborhood with intellectual parents—his father a librarian, his mother a university-educated woman from a wealthy family that lost its fortune. His mother's suicide when he was 12 was a formative trauma. He left home at 14 for Kibbutz Hulda, where the community allotted him writing time. His great-uncle Joseph Klausner's intellectual salon and library exposed him to literary culture early. He graduated from Hebrew University in 1963 and published his first book in 1965 to immediate critical acclaim.

name: Leonard Cohen
milestone_by_age_26: Published his first book of poetry, 'Let Us Compare Mythologies,' in 1956 at age 22 as the inaugural volume of the McGill Poetry Series, reviewed by Northrop Frye.
early_history_summary: Born into an Orthodox Jewish family in Westmount, Montreal, Cohen attended McGill University where he won the Chester MacNaghten Literary Competition and published his first poem in 1954. He graduated with a BA in 1955 and published his first poetry book in 1956 with help from his professor Louis Dudek. His father's will provided a modest trust income supporting his literary pursuits.
family_context_summary: Born into a prominent Jewish family in Montreal; his paternal grandfather Lyon Cohen was founding president of the Canadian Jewish Congress. His father owned a clothing store and died when Cohen was nine. His father's will provided a modest trust income that supported his early literary career.
parent_family_domain_summary: His grandfather Lyon Cohen was a prominent community leader (founding president of the Canadian Jewish Congress). His father was a clothing store owner. The family was comfortable but not wealthy; the trust income from his father's will was described as modest.
primary_early_advantage_tags: mcgill university, louis dudek mentor, irving layton mentor, trust income, chester macnaghten prize, montreal literary scene
evidence_summary: Cohen grew up in a comfortable Jewish family in Westmount, Montreal, with a prominent grandfather (Lyon Cohen, founding president of the Canadian Jewish Congress). At McGill, he was mentored by poets Irving Layton and Louis Dudek, who helped him publish his first poetry book in 1956 at age 22. His father's will provided a modest trust income allowing him to pursue writing. He won the Chester MacNaghten Literary Competition as an undergraduate. The McGill literary network was instrumental in his early publication opportunity.

name: Just Fontaine
milestone_by_age_26: Scored 13 goals in the 1958 FIFA World Cup at age 25, setting the all-time record for most goals in a single World Cup tournament that still stands today.
early_history_summary: Born in Marrakesh, Morocco, Fontaine began his amateur career at US Marocaine in 1950 at age 17, scoring 62 goals in 48 appearances. Nice recruited him in 1953 and he scored a hat trick on his France debut in December 1953 at age 20. He moved to Stade de Reims in 1956 and won the French championship in 1958 before his historic World Cup performance.
family_context_summary: Born to a French father and Spanish mother in Marrakesh, Morocco. He attended Lycée Lyautey in Casablanca. No evidence of family wealth or football connections; he was expelled from school and described as a rebellious youth who found his path through football.
primary_early_advantage_tags: moroccan league early start, nice signing, france debut hat trick, stade de reims, 1958 world cup record, professional pipeline
evidence_summary: Fontaine started playing competitively at 17 in the Moroccan top-flight, scoring 23 goals in 16 games. He was recruited by Nice in 1953 at age 20 and immediately made an impact, scoring a hat trick on his France debut. He moved to Stade de Reims in 1956, one of France's top clubs, and won the championship in 1958. His 13-goal World Cup record in 1958 at age 25 remains unbroken. No evidence of family football connections or wealth; his advantage was early professional immersion and natural scoring ability.

name: Klaus von Klitzing
milestone_by_age_26: Received his physics diploma in 1969 at age 26, a standard academic credential; his Nobel-winning discovery of the quantum Hall effect came in 1980 at age 37. No material milestone by 26 found.
early_history_summary: Born in Schroda (now Poland), von Klitzing passed the Abitur in 1962, studied physics at Braunschweig University of Technology, and received his diploma in 1969. He completed his PhD at the University of Würzburg in 1972 and habilitation in 1978 before discovering the quantum Hall effect in 1980.

name: Charlie Watts
milestone_by_age_26: Joined the Rolling Stones as drummer in January 1963 at age 21, becoming a permanent member of what would become one of the most successful rock bands in history; by 26 the band had multiple hit albums and international fame.
early_history_summary: Born in Bloomsbury, London to a lorry driver father, Watts developed a jazz obsession as a child, receiving a drum kit at 14 in 1955. He played in jazz bands from 1958, studied at Harrow Art School, and worked as a graphic designer while playing drums. He joined Blues Incorporated in 1962, then was recruited by the Rolling Stones in January 1963.
family_context_summary: Born to a lorry driver and a factory worker in Bloomsbury, London. The family lived in a prefab in Wembley that had survived Luftwaffe bombing. No evidence of family wealth or music industry connections.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. His father was a lorry driver for the London, Midland and Scottish Railway and his mother was a factory worker.
primary_early_advantage_tags: london r&b scene, alexis korner blues incorporated, rolling stones, mick jagger keith richards, ealing jazz club, british blues explosion
evidence_summary: Watts grew up in a working-class family in postwar London but was immersed in the city's vibrant jazz and blues scene. He met Alexis Korner, the godfather of British blues, who invited him to join Blues Incorporated in 1962. Through Korner's network at London's R&B clubs, Watts met Brian Jones, Mick Jagger, and Keith Richards, joining the Rolling Stones in January 1963. London's early 1960s rhythm and blues scene was a frontier ecosystem that concentrated future stars. His childhood friend Dave Green was a constant musical companion. No family wealth or music connections; his advantage was geographic and network proximity to the British blues explosion.

name: Günter Grass
milestone_by_age_26: By age 26 (Oct 1953), Grass was a student at the Berlin University of the Arts studying sculpture; his first poetry was published in 1956 (age 29) and The Tin Drum in 1959 (age 32). No material milestone by 26 found.
early_history_summary: Born in Danzig, Grass was conscripted into the Waffen-SS at 17 in 1944, wounded in 1945, and held as a US POW until 1946. He worked as a farm laborer and miner, trained as a stonemason, studied sculpture at Kunstakademie Düsseldorf (1948-52), and moved to Berlin in 1953 to study at the Berlin University of the Arts. He joined Gruppe 47 in 1955 and published his first poetry in 1956.
family_context_summary: Born to a Lutheran father and Catholic mother of Kashubian-Polish origin who ran a grocery store in Danzig-Langfuhr. Lower middle-class Catholic upbringing.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents ran a grocery store with an attached apartment. No evidence of literary or artistic family background.

name: James Dean
milestone_by_age_26: Received strong reviews for his Broadway performance as Bachir in 'The Immoralist' in February 1954 at age 23, leading Elia Kazan to cast him in 'East of Eden' during previews.
early_history_summary: Born in Indiana, Dean moved to California as a child but was sent to live with his aunt and uncle in Indiana after his mother's death when he was nine. He studied theater at UCLA, left in 1951 to pursue acting full-time, moved to New York, and was admitted to the Actors Studio to study method acting under Lee Strasberg. His Broadway role in The Immoralist in 1954 earned critical acclaim and attracted Elia Kazan's attention.
family_context_summary: Born to a farmer-turned-dental-technician father and a mother who died of cancer when Dean was nine. He was sent to live with his aunt and uncle on their farm in Fairmount, Indiana, in a Quaker household. No evidence of family wealth or entertainment connections.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. His father was a dental technician; his aunt and uncle were farmers who raised him after his mother's death.
primary_early_advantage_tags: actors studio, lee strasberg method acting, james whitmore mentor, rogers brackett patron, elia kazan, broadway
evidence_summary: Dean lost his mother at nine and was raised by his aunt and uncle in rural Indiana. He found his way to UCLA's theater program, then left to pursue acting in New York. He was admitted to the Actors Studio—one of the most selective acting institutions—where he studied method acting under Lee Strasberg alongside Marlon Brando and Julie Harris. His mentor James Whitmore and patron Rogers Brackett helped him secure Broadway roles. His acclaimed performance in The Immoralist (1954) attracted Elia Kazan, who cast him in East of Eden. His mother's death and estrangement from his father created urgency that drove his artistic intensity.

name: David Lynch
milestone_by_age_26: Made his first short film 'Six Men Getting Sick' in 1967 at age 21 as a student project; his feature debut 'Eraserhead' was released in 1977 at age 31. No material independently verifiable milestone by 26 found.
early_history_summary: Born in Missoula, Montana to a USDA research scientist father, Lynch studied painting at Corcoran School of Art and the School of the Museum of Fine Arts Boston before enrolling at the Pennsylvania Academy of the Fine Arts. He made his first short film in 1967 at age 21 and began working on Eraserhead around 1972, completing it in 1977.
family_context_summary: Born to a USDA research scientist father and an English-language tutor mother. The family moved frequently due to the father's USDA assignments. Middle-class upbringing in small-town America.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a USDA research scientist; mother was an English-language tutor. No evidence of film or arts industry connections. A family friend, Bushnell Keeler (a painter), gave Lynch a copy of 'The Art Spirit' which inspired him to pursue art.
